source_metadata.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization

atoms.canonical_statement: The study reframes robustness to misleading context as selective trust and aims to measure and improve whether models reject misleading signals while preserving useful-context behavior.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We recast the problem as selective trust and introduce MIST ... We then propose SCOPE ...

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors define useful selective trust as jointly rejecting misleading signals, benefiting from correct context, and remaining unaffected by irrelevant context without sacrificing clean reasoning.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A genuinely useful reasoning model ... must do three things at once: reject a misleading signal ... benefit from context that is actually correct, and stay unmoved by irrelevant context.

atoms.canonical_statement: MIST-1000 contains 1,000 source items, including 800 adapted from existing QA, math, and reasoning benchmarks and 200 newly human-authored challenging scenarios.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We release a pool of 1,000 source items: 800 adapted from existing question-answering (QA), math, and reasoning benchmarks, and 200 written by annotators ...

population.label: MIST-1000 source items

atoms.canonical_statement: Each MIST item is rendered under four matched conditions: clean, misleading, correct-context, and irrelevant-context.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Each item is rendered under four matched conditions. The clean condition adds no context; the misleading condition adds a signal toward a wrong answer; the correct-context condition ...; and the irrelevant-context condition ...

atoms.canonical_statement: Across the four MIST conditions, the question, answer space, answer type, gold answer, and plausible wrong answer are held fixed; only the added context changes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Only the added context changes: the question, answer space, answer type, gold answer, and plausible wrong answer are held fixed across all four conditions.

atoms.canonical_statement: MIST annotation used STEM-trained annotators in a two-pass process with independent verification of answer validity, wrong-answer plausibility, naturalness, ambiguity, answer leakage, and formatting.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Our annotators, each holding at least a bachelor’s degree in a ... STEM field, built the benchmark in two passes ... A second pass verified answer validity, wrong-answer plausibility, naturalness, ambiguity, answer leakage ... and formatting.

atoms.canonical_statement: MIST spans math, general knowledge, science, commonsense, academic, consumer-finance, and workplace-policy topics; includes multiple-choice, numeric, and boolean answers; and balances misleading contexts across nine source channels and seven wrong-answer plausibility classes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The pool spans math, general knowledge, science, commonsense, academic, consumer-finance, and workplace-policy topics, and mixes multiple-choice, numeric, and boolean formats ... balanced across nine source channels and wrong answers span seven plausibility classes.

atoms.canonical_statement: Because 800 MIST items are adapted from public benchmarks, some evaluated base models may have seen the underlying clean questions; MIST is therefore not intended as a pure unseen-knowledge test.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Because 800 items are adapted from public benchmarks, some base models may have seen the underlying clean questions, so our benchmark is not intended as a pure unseen-knowledge test.

atoms.canonical_statement: The main MIST evaluation reports clean, misleading, correct-context, irrelevant-context, and overall accuracy together with SC2W.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The paper-facing main table reports Clean Acc., Misleading Acc., Correct-Context Acc., Irrelevant Acc., Overall Acc., and SC2W.

atoms.canonical_statement: SC2W is the proportion of items answered correctly in the clean condition that become incorrect under the matched misleading condition.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The central susceptibility metric is signal-induced correct-to-wrong flipping ... It conditions on items the model can already solve, thereby isolating the failures caused specifically by the misleading condition.

outcome.definition: P(clean correct and misleading wrong) divided by P(clean correct), evaluated within matched items.
outcome.measurement_method: Paired deterministic final-answer correctness across clean and misleading conditions.

atoms.canonical_statement: Main MIST correctness is scored deterministically by type-aware final-answer parsing rather than by an LLM judge.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The main MIST metrics are computed without an LLM judge. For each model generation, we parse the final answer and compare it against the gold answer ...

atoms.canonical_statement: MIST numeric answers are compared after final numeric extraction with tolerance 1e-4, multiple-choice answers as option letters, and boolean answers after yes/no normalization; unparsable outputs are marked incorrect.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The scorer is type-aware: numeric answers are compared after extracting the final numeric value with a tolerance of 10−4; multiple-choice answers are compared as option letters; and boolean answers are normalized to yes/no. If the final answer cannot be parsed, the row is marked incorrect ...

atoms.canonical_statement: SCOPE mines items for which a base model is correct on the clean prompt but wrong on the matched misleading prompt.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: SCOPE ... mines the failures that matter: items a base model answers correctly on its own but gets wrong once a misleading signal is added.

atoms.canonical_statement: For each retained SCOPE item, the preference pair contains a truth-consistent full-completion response r+ and the base model’s signal-following wrong full-completion response r-.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For each mined item i, we form a single counterfactual response pair, i.e., a correct full-completion response r+ ... and the base model’s signal-following wrong full-completion response r− ...

atoms.canonical_statement: SCOPE reuses the same chosen/rejected response pair across misleading, clean, correct-context, and irrelevant-context prompts for the same underlying item.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: ... and pair it with the four matched context prompts ... Because all four comparisons share the same underlying problem, response pair, and format, the learning signal is tied to the context’s role ...

atoms.canonical_statement: SCOPE chooses r+ from the base model’s clean-condition correct response when available and otherwise uses a correct diagnostic response from the same frozen base checkpoint; r- is the base model’s naturally terminated wrong misleading-context response.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The rejected response r− is the same base model’s naturally terminated, non-truncated wrong response under the misleading condition. The chosen response r+ ... use that base model’s clean-condition correct response when available; otherwise fall back to a correct diagnostic response generated by the same frozen base checkpoint ...

atoms.canonical_statement: SCOPE applies leakage and quality filters to diagnostic fallback responses, including removal of privileged-note or answer-key wording, malformed or truncated generations, duplicate chosen/rejected responses, incomplete condition sets, and response pairs with the same final answer.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The leakage filter removes completions that mention hidden-note provenance or phrases such as “teacher note”, “reference solution”, “gold answer”, or “answer key”. We also drop malformed generations, overlong responses, incomplete condition sets, duplicated chosen/rejected responses, and rows where the chosen and rejected responses collapse to the same final answer.

atoms.canonical_statement: Headline SCOPE training assigns 25% sampling mass to each of the misleading, clean, correct-context, and irrelevant-context preference sets.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In all headline runs, we use equal condition sampling ... which assigns 25% sampling mass to each of Dmis, Dclean, Dcor, and Dirr.

atoms.canonical_statement: SCOPE uses standard full-completion sigmoid DPO; the claimed methodological novelty is the matched, balanced preference-data construction rather than a new preference loss or optimizer.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Our method uses standard full-completion DPO ... the novelty lies entirely in the matched, balanced preference data rather than the optimizer.

atoms.canonical_statement: The SCOPE training pool and the 1,000-item MIST evaluation pool are item-disjoint.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: SCOPE uses a training pool that is item-disjoint from the 1,000-item evaluation pool.

atoms.canonical_statement: The SCOPE source training pool contains 5,000 source items rendered under four conditions, yielding 20,000 condition rows before mining.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We first build 5,000 training source items, each rendered under the same four context conditions ... This gives 20,000 condition rows before mining.

atoms.canonical_statement: The retained Qwen3-4B SCOPE training set contains 1,393 quartets (5,572 rows), with r+ sourced from 1,311 clean responses and 82 diagnostic responses.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The retained Qwen3-4B training set contains 1,393 quartets (5,572 rows), with r+ sourced from 1,311 clean responses and 82 diagnostic responses.

atoms.canonical_statement: The retained Llama-3.2-3B SCOPE training set contains 2,360 quartets (9,440 rows), with r+ sourced from 1,473 clean responses and 887 diagnostic responses.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The retained Llama-3.2-3B set contains 2,360 quartets (9,440 rows), with r+ sourced from 1,473 clean responses and 887 diagnostic responses.

atoms.canonical_statement: DPO-based trainable methods use beta 0.1, learning rate 5e-6, cosine decay, warmup ratio 0.1, max gradient norm 1.0, max sequence length 4096, batch size 4, gradient accumulation 8, bf16, gradient checkpointing, seed 0, and a fixed 300-step training budget.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For DPO-based trainable methods, we use ... β = 0.1, learning rate 5 × 10−6, cosine decay, warmup ratio 0.1, maximum gradient norm 1.0, maximum sequence length 4096 ... per-device batch size 4, gradient accumulation 8, bfloat16 ... seed 0. The main method-comparison runs use a fixed 300-step training budget ...

atoms.canonical_statement: Parameter-efficient training uses LoRA rank 64 and alpha 128 on q, k, v, o, gate, up, and down projections; all trainable experiments ran on eight NVIDIA A800 GPUs and most training runs took about three hours.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The parameter-efficient implementation uses low-rank adaptation (LoRA) ... with rank 64 and alpha 128 on ... q, k, v, o, gate, up, and down projections ... All trainable experiments were run on a node with eight NVIDIA A800 GPUs, and most training runs completed in approximately three hours.

atoms.canonical_statement: MIST experiments use the 1,000-item matched pool with a single fixed decoding seed; Base and SCOPE uncertainty is estimated by item-level bootstrap resampling, while auxiliary defense rows use approximate proxy uncertainty when exact per-item artifacts are unavailable.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All experiments on our benchmark use the 1,000-item matched pool with a single fixed decoding seed ... base and SCOPE rows use standard deviations from item-level bootstrap resampling, and auxiliary defense rows use the approximate proxy estimates ... when exact per-item artifacts are unavailable.

atoms.canonical_statement: On Qwen3-4B and Llama-3.2-3B, SCOPE is compared with Prompt-defense, SFT, misleading-only Standard-DPO, and on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) under the same four MIST conditions.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: On the two trainable bases (Qwen3-4B and Llama-3.2-3B), we compare our method against four mitigations ... Prompt-defense ... SFT ... Standard-DPO ... and on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) ...

atoms.canonical_statement: Across 23 frontier and open-weight models, a misleading signal reduced accuracy by 17.1 percentage points on average.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Susceptibility proves universal: across 23 frontier and open-weight models, a single misleading signal costs 17.1 points on average.

population.label: Frontier and open-weight models evaluated on MIST

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors conclude that reasoning models should be trained and evaluated for selective trust rather than resistance to external context alone.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Reliable reasoning models should be trained and judged on selective trust, not resistance alone.

atoms.canonical_statement: MIST is a controlled, text-only diagnostic, so its susceptibility rates should not be interpreted as deployment prevalence.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Our benchmark is a controlled, text-only diagnostic: its rates measure susceptibility, not deployment prevalence ...

atoms.canonical_statement: The mitigation experiments cover only two trainable model families, leaving broader architectures and model scales untested.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: ... our two-family mitigation leaves broader architectures and scales untested.

atoms.canonical_statement: Robustness under matched MIST prompts does not establish chain-of-thought faithfulness.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Robustness under matched prompts is not evidence of chain-of-thought faithfulness ...

atoms.canonical_statement: Benchmark contamination cannot be fully excluded because most items are adapted from public benchmarks, although SC2W conditions on clean-correct behavior.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: ... as most items are adapted from public benchmarks, contamination cannot be fully excluded, though conditioning SC2W on clean-correct behavior mitigates it.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors caution that because MIST intentionally embeds incorrect signals, its measured rates should not be read as natural failure frequencies.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Our benchmark intentionally embeds incorrect signals to stress-test reliability, so its rates should not be read as natural failure frequencies.
